entrypoints.summary: Chosen or forged Kyber ciphertexts are supplied to decapsulation; the report describes repeated ciphertext choices targeted to secret positions and timing of their handling.
The patched AArch64 implementation exposes secret-coefficient conversion through poly_tomsg and compression through poly_compress; the patch removes their division expressions.

affected_components.role: Rendered patch shows division-based coefficient conversion replaced by reciprocal-multiply arithmetic and a conditional-move-based message conversion; analogous AArch64 parameter-set files are listed in the commit.

code_slices.fixed: The rendered post-patch poly_tomsg path shifts t, adds 1665, multiplies by 80635, shifts right by 28, and masks one bit. The displayed compression path applies equivalent bounded arithmetic before packing.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The commit is titled as a port of KyberSlash fixes to AArch64 and changes 18 files across the Kyber512, Kyber768, and Kyber1024 AArch64 directories.
code_slices.vulnerable: The rendered pre-patch code in poly_tomsg computes (((t << 1) + KYBER_Q / 2) / KYBER_Q) & 1; the displayed pre-patch compression calculation also uses a shifted, rounded numerator divided by KYBER_Q.

negative_controls: No run result is supplied for PQClean AArch64.
No claim is made that the patch replacement is timing-safe on every architecture/compiler.
observability.positive_marker: Timing observations match the division-timing model sufficiently to identify secret-key hypotheses; the reported demos stop after a recomputed public key matches.

preconditions: A target performs vulnerable Kyber decapsulation on attacker-supplied ciphertexts.
The attacker can obtain sufficiently stable decapsulation timing measurements.
The target platform/compiler realization has operand-dependent division timing for the relevant secret-derived arithmetic.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Multiple ciphertext choices targeting each secret position; the paper describes repeated trials and timing aggregation.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit selected ciphertexts repeatedly for decapsulation and collect timing observations used to distinguish secret-key hypotheses.

mitigations.concept: reciprocal-multiply replacement for secret coefficient conversion

relation_candidates.rationale: Repeated chosen ciphertext handling and measurement exposes decapsulation timings to the attacker.
The pre-patch conversion expressions perform division by KYBER_Q on numerators derived from secret-influenced coefficients, providing the variable-time operation underlying the timing oracle.
The reported attack compares repeated timing measurements with models of division timings for secret-key possibilities.
The paper and demo descriptions report complete secret-key recovery in their demonstrated reference-code environments.

relation_candidates.dst: reciprocal-multiply replacement for secret coefficient conversion
relation_candidates.rationale: The patch removes the displayed divisions by KYBER_Q and substitutes bounded shift/add/multiply/shift arithmetic.

impact.affected_asset: Confidentiality of the Kyber/ML-KEM secret key.
impact.attacker_capability: Submit selected ciphertexts to a decapsulation-capable target repeatedly and measure its response time.
impact.security_effect: Timing side channel that can disclose Kyber secret-key information and, in the report's demonstrated reference-code environments, enable complete secret-key recovery.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker repeatedly submits selected Kyber ciphertexts for decapsulation and records decapsulation timing; the demonstration procedure uses ciphertext choices targeting secret-key positions.

Secret-influenced polynomial coefficients are transformed into shifted and rounded numerators for division by KYBER_Q in message conversion and compression, so secret data reaches an operation whose latency is not required to be input-independent.

The concrete hazardous operation is integer division of a secret-derived numerator by the public Kyber modulus: the pre-patch poly_tomsg expression divides ((t << 1) + KYBER_Q/2) by KYBER_Q, and pre-patch compression similarly divides a shifted, rounded coefficient by KYBER_Q.

Operand-dependent division timing provides a quantitative decapsulation-time oracle. The report and linked demos describe recovery of complete Kyber secret keys on demonstrated reference-code environments; this bundle does not independently demonstrate recovery against a built PQClean AArch64 binary.

failure.operation: integer division by KYBER_Q of a secret-derived coefficient numerator during message conversion or compression

primary_invariant.statement: Arithmetic operations on secret-derived Kyber coefficients in decapsulation must not expose operand-dependent execution time to a timing observer.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-patch coefficient conversions divide secret-derived shifted and rounded numerators by KYBER_Q; the KyberSlash report identifies secret-dependent division timing as observable through decapsulation.

quality.review_notes: The immutable PQClean patch directly establishes division removal in the AArch64 source paths. The paper and demo index establish measured/reproducible key-recovery claims for reference-code deployments on Raspberry Pi 2 and Cortex-M4, not an independently measured PQClean AArch64 executable. The supplied bundle does not include a downloaded demo/test harness or a PQClean timing trace/run result, so no executable oracle is asserted. Timing safety of the replacement remains target and compiler dependent.

remediation.invariant_restored: The AArch64 patch replaces displayed division-based coefficient conversions with shift/add/reciprocal-multiply/shift arithmetic (including multiplier 80635), removing those secret-derived division expressions from the patched paths.
mitigation_classes: constant-time conditional move for message-to-polynomial conversion

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The reported procedure repeats selected ciphertext handling, aggregates timing observations, and compares them against timing models for secret-key possibilities.
data_structure_invariants: Polynomial coefficients used in secret-key-dependent decapsulation conversion must not drive variable-latency arithmetic observable through request timing.
KYBER_Q is a public fixed divisor, but the numerator produced from the coefficient is secret-influenced.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The attacker controls ciphertext selection but not the secret coefficient; timing classification is based on repeated measurements.
numeric_domains.name: coefficient-conversion numerator
numeric_domains.signedness: mixed: source coefficient is int16_t and patched conversion temporaries are uint32_t/int32_t

state_context.state_machine: A decapsulation invocation processes an attacker-selected ciphertext through secret-dependent polynomial conversion and returns an externally measurable completion time.

target.component: AArch64 Kyber512, Kyber768, and Kyber1024 polynomial message conversion and compression paths
